0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Level 3 is the richest tier of the Loire Valley — from dry Chenin Blanc on the Anjou schist slopes, to top botrytised wines of the Layon valley, to the flinty twin stars of Sancerre, you have travelled through dozens of white and sparkling AOCs. This assessment tests your grasp of the whole Chenin Blanc craft spectrum, soil recognition in the Centre-Loire, and the principles of Loire food pairing.

📝 Scope of the assessment

All 11 lessons of Level 3 (lo-l3-1 ~ lo-l3-11), covering dozens of white/sparkling AOCs

🎯 Number of questions

5 comprehensive questions, covering Chenin Blanc's sweetness system, noble-rot science, Sancerre geology and pairing principles

🏆 Pass mark

Answer 4 or more correctly (80%) to unlock Level 4
1.title: Level 3 Comprehensive Assessment
1.questions.0.question: In the Vouvray sweetness system, what is the usual residual-sugar range of "Moelleux"?
1.questions.0.explanation: Under EU labelling rules, Vouvray sweetness levels are: Sec (0–4 g/L), Demi-Sec (4–12 g/L), Moelleux (12–45 g/L), Doux/Liquoreux (above 45 g/L, noble rot or very sweet). Moelleux means "soft," and denotes a balanced sweet style with obvious sweetness that still keeps Chenin Blanc's high acidity.
1.questions.1.question: What is the most important winemaking feature of Muscadet Sèvre et Maine sur Lie?
1.questions.1.options.0: Aged at least 18 months in new oak barrels
1.questions.1.options.1: Aged on the dead-yeast sediment (lees) for at least 6 months before bottling, giving yeasty bread notes and a fine texture
1.questions.1.options.3: Fermentation must be completed in underground tuffeau caves
1.questions.1.explanation: "Sur Lie" is Muscadet's most important quality mark — the wine is aged on dead yeast sediment (lees) (at least 6 months, up to 20+ months for top wines), and yeast autolysis gives bread crumb, cream and a slight sparkle (CO₂ retained), greatly raising palate complexity and texture.
1.questions.2.question: What is the most fundamental reason Sancerre × Crottin de Chavignol is called the "textbook of terroir pairing"?
1.questions.2.options.0: Because both begin with "S," which makes them easy to remember
1.questions.2.options.1: Both come from the same Chavignol area, coexisting on the same land and in the same food culture, forming a deep "terroir resonance"
1.questions.2.options.2: Because the cheese's high fat content makes drinkers less likely to get drunk when drinking more Sancerre
1.questions.2.options.3: The law requires Sancerre to be sold together with Crottin
1.questions.2.explanation: The deepest reason is "terroir pairing" — Crottin and Sancerre both come from the Chavignol area and have been paired by locals for centuries; this common origin creates the most natural harmony.
1.questions.3.question: Which of the following most accurately describes the characteristics of Savennières AOC?
1.questions.3.options.0: Made from Sauvignon Blanc, with a style similar to Sancerre
1.questions.3.options.1: Dry white made from 100% Chenin Blanc, on the Anjou schist slopes, where Nicolas Joly's biodynamic farming has made it one of the world's top white wines
1.questions.3.options.2: Mainly produces Cabernet Franc reds, the most expensive red AOC in Anjou
1.questions.3.options.3: Made from Melon de Bourgogne, with the same style as Muscadet
1.questions.3.explanation: Savennières AOC makes dry white from 100% Chenin Blanc, on mixed schist (schiste) and volcanic-rock slopes in western Anjou. Nicolas Joly's Clos de la Coulée de Serrant (biodynamic farming) is the best-known producer and is considered one of the world's greatest dry white wines.
1.questions.4.question: What is the most critical difference between Pouilly-Fumé and Pouilly-sur-Loire?
1.questions.4.options.0: They are exactly the same AOC, just with different names
1.questions.4.options.1: Pouilly-Fumé uses Sauvignon Blanc (higher quality), Pouilly-sur-Loire uses Chasselas (simpler quality), and both come from the same land
1.questions.4.options.2: Pouilly-Fumé is from southern France, Pouilly-sur-Loire from the north
1.questions.4.options.3: Pouilly-sur-Loire is sweet, Pouilly-Fumé is dry
1.questions.4.explanation: Pouilly-Fumé AOC (Sauvignon Blanc) and Pouilly-sur-Loire AOC (Chasselas) come from exactly the same geographic area (the town of Pouilly-sur-Loire in the Nièvre department), but use different varieties: Pouilly-Fumé uses Sauvignon Blanc and is the top AOC; Pouilly-sur-Loire uses Chasselas, has a simpler style, and is now almost abandoned, with an ever-shrinking area.
